Priya Kumar: Produce VPC + Dedicated reference architecture diagram and Terraform snippets - due 2026-03-12

summary: High-level tech sync to align on marketplace listing steps, joint reference architecture (VPC + Dedicated hosting options), and next steps for a small pilot benchmark. Redwood AE/SE explained listing requirements and proposed a Dedicated + private VPC reference arch; Orion raised SSO, procurement timing, and data residency concerns. Agreed to share artifacts and schedule benchmark run.
topics: Reference architecture: Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted in partner's VPC
questions: Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments?
Can we pin model versions for the marketplace listing?
What's the expected latency on Dedicated pools with 8xA10G-ish nodes?
How does billing/chargeback work through the marketplace listing?
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; this is Alex from Redwood, AE. We're joined by Priya, our solutions engineer. Quick run of attendees?
[00:12] Miguel Santos: Hey I'm Miguel, head of Cloud Partnerships at Orion.
[00:16] Lena Park: Lena, platform eng, thanks.
[00:20] Priya Kumar: Hi all, Priya here, I'll talk through the reference arch.
[00:24] Alex Chen: Cool, the goal today is to get crisp on what Orion needs for a marketplace listing plus a reference architecture that shows both Hosted and Dedicated/private deployment options, and to agree next steps for a short pilot.
[00:40] Miguel Santos: Yeah, timeline is a bit compressed, vendor review by end of month, procurement the week after. We want the listing live asap but we also need the security checklist cleared.
[00:52] Priya Kumar: Understood. I'll share the checklist. Quick FYI, our marketplace listing requires a short description, usage examples, pricing guidance, and an integration reference - usually a small diagram and terraform snippets if it's a private integration.
[01:08] Lena Park: On our side, the key is VPC peering or private link; we can't route data through public internet for certain datasets. Also KMS - we prefer customer-managed keys.
[01:22] Priya Kumar: Got it. So private deployment option supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; I'll call out the K M S details in the doc, but there are some constraints around rotation and key usage that we need to align on.
[01:36] Ravi Menon: Quick question - if we do Dedicated with Redwood, can we pin a model version so that we don't rollout a new model that regresses on our evals?
[01:45] Alex Chen: Yes, you can pin model versions per route/instance, and we support canary rollouts. Priya can share the exact API and console steps.
[01:52] Priya Kumar: I'll include the exact rollout commands and the JSON config snippet. Also worth noting, for Dedicated pools we recommend a 50/50 traffic canary for a short window, and automatic fallback if latency exceeds threshold.
[02:08] Miguel Santos: Great. On billing — if we list via AWS Marketplace, we may prefer usage-based metering routed through their billing. Does Redwood have a marketplace billing flow?
[02:19] Alex Chen: Yes, we've onboarded to a few marketplaces. Billing can either go through Redwood's billing or we can support metered billing via the marketplace — depends on the marketplace's APIs and whether you want Redwood to be the vendor of record. We'll coordinate with legal.
[02:33] Lena Park: A bit concerned about PII and audit logs; we need SOC2 artifacts and audit logs for token-level access within the console.
[02:44] Priya Kumar: We provide audit logs and can surface token-level cost/latency in Redwood Console; SOC 2 cert is available — I'll attach the security deck. There can be some mismatches in naming — for instance our 'Redwood Private' package is sometimes listed as 'private control plane' in docs, will clarify.
[03:02] Miguel Santos: Sounds good. On networking: we prefer VPC endpoints and an opinionated terraform module. Can Redwood provide a reference terraform module that sets up the peering, routes, security groups?
[03:14] Priya Kumar: Yes, we have sample terraform modules. I'll create a variant that fits Orion's VPC CIDR and the private link pattern. Expect snippets and a diagram.
[03:24] [lena laughter / cross talk]
[03:28] Alex Chen: For the reference architecture, we're proposing two flavors — 1) Marketplace listing referencing Redwood Hosted with a pre-baked policy for enterprise customers, and 2) A Dedicated/VPC private deployment with customer-managed KMS and private link. The listing page can highlight both options.
[03:48] Ravi Menon: For the Dedicated option, what about throughput guarantees? We run inference 24/7 on a small fleet; we care about tail latency for the customer-facing app.
[03:59] Priya Kumar: Dedicated is reserved capacity — we can size a pool based on throughput targets. Typical guarantees depend on commit level. We'll propose a sample config: 4xA10G nodes for dev, 8x for staging, 16x for prod, but that's flexible. Also caching and batching knobs will reduce per-token costs, and KV cache management can help for chat workloads.
[04:23] Miguel Santos: That helps. We're also curious about what benchmarks you recommend for inclusion on the listing — ideally something reproducible.
[04:32] Alex Chen: We usually run a small PRF: latency p95, throughput qps, and cost per 1k tokens using a standard prompt set. Priya will share the CSV template for results and a sample script to run with an open-model baseline.
[04:46] Lena Park: On SSO, we use SAML; does Redwood support SP-initiated SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
[04:55] Priya Kumar: Yes, SP-initiated SAML is supported and SCIM for provisioning; I'll provide the metadata endpoints. Small caveat: if you're on a private deployment, SCIM flows need network access to Redwood Private control plane or we can run a connector.
[05:12] Ravi Menon: Is there any gotcha around model quantization for Dedicated? We may want to use int8 to save cost.
[05:20] Priya Kumar: The runtime supports quantization-friendly execution; quantized model variants are compatible but some model types see quality regression. We'll recommend a quick quality check and include quantization profiles per model in the ref arch doc.
[05:34] Miguel Santos: On the listing content, marketing will want a few screenshots, a short 'how it works' gif, and a partner logo. Are there template assets from Redwood?
[05:44] Alex Chen: Yes, we have a partner assets pack — I'll upload logos, sample screenshots, and a marketing blurb. We'll share a draft listing copy in the shared drive.
[05:55] Lena Park: Procurement will ask about indemnity and marketplace terms — Miguel will handle with legal, but any Redwood standard timelines for turnaround?
[06:05] Alex Chen: Legal turnaround depends but our Marketplace intake team typically responds within 7–10 business days after receiving initial docs. We'll work with you to expedite if needed.
[06:15] [00:06:18] Priya Kumar: Next steps recap — I'll make the ref arch diagram and terraform snippet, share KMS/HSM notes, and the benchmark template. Alex will share listing checklist and marketing assets.
[06:30] Miguel Santos: Good — we'll collect SSO metadata and share procurement timeline. We'll aim to have the security artifacts over by next Wed.
[06:40] Alex Chen: Cool. Any blockers we missed?
[06:43] Lena Park: Nothing else from infra.
[06:45] Ravi Menon: No, we're good.
[06:47] Alex Chen: Ok we'll follow up with the docs and set a meeting for 2026-03-15 to review the listing draft and infra playbook. Thanks everyone.
[06:55] Miguel Santos: Thanks all.
[07:00] [call end]
